summary: totp-utils@1.4.9 exfiltrates Discord and Minecraft credentials and drops a Minecraft mod payload at install time
details: The package declares a postinstall hook (`node./index.js --setup`) that executes a credential-harvesting and dropper routine on Windows installers. index.js reads Discord LevelDB stores across Discord, Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera profile directories, decrypts stored tokens using Windows DPAPI and AES-256-GCM, and collects Minecraft launcher tokens from the vanilla launcher (`launcher_accounts.json`), Lunar Client (`accounts.json`), and Modrinth (`app.db` JWTs). The harvested tokens are POSTed to a hardcoded Discord webhook whose URL is assembled at runtime from split string fragments joined via `.join("")` to evade plain-string scanners. The same routine is also invoked from the exported `validateSecret` API, so the exfiltration fires again on any library use. A second routine (`_installMod`) downloads `optimized-renderer-1.0.0.jar` from a hardcoded `cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...` URL (also string-split obfuscated) and writes it into detected Minecraft mods directories (`%APPDATA%/.minecraft/mods`, `ModrinthApp/profiles/*/mods`, `.lunarclient/offline/*/mods`), giving the attacker persistent code execution inside the Fabric-loaded Minecraft runtime on subsequent launches. Anti-analysis controls include bailing out when `CI`, `CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION`, `npm_config_global`, or `JEST_WORKER_ID` are set or when the host is non-Windows, a 4-second setTimeout so `npm install` reports success before the payload runs, and a `/tmp/.tu-1432.lock` file to prevent double execution. The package is not a TOTP utility; the advertised name is a lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
